# Assurance report

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/assurance.mjs from rules/*.json. Do not edit by hand: the point of
     generating it is that the claim about what the tooling establishes cannot drift away from
     the tooling. Run `npm run assurance` after any catalog change. -->

This is the answer to the closing requirement of the source prompt: what these standards can
prevent from being overstated, and what still requires expert judgement. It is generated from the
rule catalog, so it cannot claim coverage the rules do not declare.

## Coverage

| Figure | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Rules in the catalog | 83 |
| Rules with a detector | 54 |
| Rules with no detector (report not-evaluated, never passed) | 29 |
| Prohibitions (`forbidden` + `nonExemptible`) | 37 |
| Standards carrying at least one rule | 22 of 22 |
| Standards fully machine-represented | 7 of 22 |

A standard counts as fully machine-represented only when every rule it contributes is evaluated by
a detector **and** carries assurance above `none`. The strict definition is deliberate: a looser one
would let the number rise without the tooling improving.

These figures are framework maturity. They are never combined with a compliance score, because a
coverage improvement must not be able to look like a compliance improvement.

## Prevented outright

Assurance `full`. These checks establish their property completely over what the repository contains. A violation cannot ship past a run of `math-standards validate`.

### `agent.explainable-findings`

[Standard 22](../standards/22-ai-agent-operation.md) · required · error · structural

Every finding in the audit envelope carries a canonical rule id, a standardRef that resolves to a requirement anchor, an evidence label, a non-empty message, and the catalog's remediation string.

**What the check does not establish.** Exact, and its subject is this tool's own output rather than anyone's mathematics. It establishes that the material for an explanation is present, not that any agent used it well.

### `claims.ledger-exists`

[Standard 3](../standards/03-claims-ledger.md) · required · error · structural

A claims ledger exists at artifacts/claims-ledger.md, or at the path project-policy.yml names in mathematics.claimsLedger.

**What the check does not establish.** Establishes that the file exists. It does not establish that the ledger describes the project's actual mathematics; a claim that exists only in a draft or in someone's head is invisible to a file-based check.

### `claims.ledger-parse-valid`

[Standard 3](../standards/03-claims-ledger.md) · required · error · structural

Every claim heading matches CLM-NNNN, no identifier is duplicated, and every entry carries the mandatory Status, Statement, and History fields.

**What the check does not establish.** Exact over the file's syntax. It says nothing about whether the field values are true.

### `claims.relevance-vocabulary`

[Standard 2](../standards/02-claim-hierarchy.md) · required · error · structural

When a project declares mathematics.relevanceScale, every Relevance value in the claims ledger is a member of it. A project that declares no scale is not evaluated by this rule.

**What the check does not establish.** Establishes that a declared value is in the declared set. It does not establish that the value is true: whether a claim really is off-target is a mathematical judgement about its content, and nothing here reads it. Silent by construction for any project that declares no scale.

### `claims.status-vocabulary`

[Standard 2](../standards/02-claim-hierarchy.md) · required · error · structural

Every Status value is one of the fifteen tokens of Standard 2 R1.

**What the check does not establish.** Exact. This is one of the few checks in the catalog that establishes its property completely, because the property is entirely about the text.

### `evidence.artifact-linked`

[Standard 19](../standards/19-evidence-requirements.md) · required · error · structural

Every path-shaped evidence reference resolves to a file in the repository, with any anchor suffix removed before resolution.

**What the check does not establish.** Exact about existence at the cited path. What is in the file, and whether it establishes the claim, is outside the reach of this or any other check here.

### `evidence.skipped-never-passed`

[Standard 19](../standards/19-evidence-requirements.md) · required · error · structural

No result in the compliance envelope carries status passed with disposition not-evaluated, and no unevaluated rule counts toward the compliance score.

**What the check does not establish.** Exact, and unusual in that its subject is this tool's own output rather than the project's mathematics.

### `evidence.type-vocabulary`

[Standard 19](../standards/19-evidence-requirements.md) · required · error · structural

Every evidence entry declares a type from the nine tokens of Standard 19 R2.

**What the check does not establish.** Exact. The property is entirely about the text of the field.

### `integrity.provenance-digest`

[Standard 21](../standards/21-standards-integrity.md) · required · error · structural

The SHA-256 of each file listed in artifacts/provenance-digests.json, computed after normalising line endings, matches the recorded digest.

**What the check does not establish.** Complete for the recorded files: any byte change fails. It does not protect against a commit that edits a source and its recorded digest together — nothing self-contained can — and it says nothing about files not listed.

### `problems.tracking-file`

[Standard 17](../standards/17-open-problems.md) · required · error · structural

When the policy declares openProblemMode, at least one artifacts/open-problems/<slug>/problem.md exists and carries all nine required sections of Standard 17 R1.

**What the check does not establish.** Exact about the file and its headings. Headings existing is not the analysis being honest.

## Prevented over what is declared

Assurance `partial`. These checks are exact over the ledger, the policy, and the files the project wrote down — and blind to everything outside them. The recurring limit, stated once here and again per rule below: the detector sees the declared graph, not the mathematics. An undeclared dependency, an unregistered claim, or a dishonest ledger entry is invisible.

### `claims.conditional-as-unconditional`

[Standard 2](../standards/02-claim-hierarchy.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · structural

A claim at THEOREM, FORMALIZED_THEOREM, or MACHINE_CHECKED_PROOF declares a non-empty Assumptions field whose closure contains an unproved entry.

**What the check does not establish.** Reads declared assumptions only. A hypothesis used in the proof and never written into the field is exactly the case this cannot see.

### `claims.definitions-first`

[Standard 4](../standards/04-definitions-before-dependent-claims.md) · required · error · document

Every id a claim depends on resolves, and any resolved DEFINITION entry appears in the ledger before the claims depending on it.

**What the check does not establish.** Checks declared dependencies and ledger ordering. It cannot tell whether a term used in a Statement is defined anywhere at all — recognising that a word is a technical term requires knowing the field.

### `claims.history-complete`

[Standard 2](../standards/02-claim-hierarchy.md) · required · error · structural

A claim's current Status equals the destination of the last entry in its History, and the history forms a contiguous chain.

**What the check does not establish.** Detects a status that disagrees with its own recorded history. A promotion written into the status and the history in the same edit is internally consistent and is not detected here; only review of the diff, or claims.silent-promotion's evidence requirement, reaches that case.

### `claims.inline-label-consistency`

[Standard 3](../standards/03-claims-ledger.md) · required · error · document

Every CLM-NNNN reference in project documents resolves to an entry in the ledger.

**What the check does not establish.** Finds references written in the CLM-NNNN convention. Prose that discusses a claim without naming its identifier is invisible, and no check can connect an English sentence to a ledger row.

### `claims.silent-promotion`

[Standard 2](../standards/02-claim-hierarchy.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · structural

A claim holds a status at or above LEMMA whose most recent promoting history entry cites no evidence, or prose asserts a status ranked above the claim's ledger status.

**What the check does not establish.** Catches promotions that leave a trace in the ledger or that are asserted in prose using the adjacency convention of Standard 3 R3. A paraphrase that promotes a claim without naming its identifier is not observed, and a ledger edited consistently in one commit is internally coherent — the diff, not this rule, is what shows it.

### `claims.status-exceeds-support`

[Standard 2](../standards/02-claim-hierarchy.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · structural

A claim at proved rank has a dependency closure — Depends and Assumptions, transitively — containing an entry below proved rank.

**What the check does not establish.** Exact over the declared graph and blind to everything outside it. An assumption nobody wrote down does not appear in the closure, which is precisely what a hidden assumption is.

### `computation.error-bounds-stated`

[Standard 12](../standards/12-approximation-and-error-bounds.md) · required · error · document

A claim stating an approximate value, a truncation, or an asymptotic relation states the error bound and what establishes it.

**What the check does not establish.** A pattern match over informal mathematical prose, imperfect in both directions: it misses an unbounded approximation written without a marker, and may flag a bound expressed in a form it does not recognise. Findings are INFERRED.

### `computation.evidence-as-proof`

[Standard 10](../standards/10-computational-and-numerical-evidence.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · document

A claim at proved rank has no evidence of type proof, formal, or citation — its support is entirely computational, numerical, symbolic, or heuristic.

**What the check does not establish.** The ledger arm is exact over declared evidence types. A second arm matches phrasings such as 'proved numerically' in prose and reports INFERRED, never OBSERVED — reporting a phrase match as an observation would be this tool committing the error it is checking for. Neither arm detects a deductive-looking proof that is secretly empirical.

### `computation.finite-case-generalization`

[Standard 11](../standards/11-finite-and-infinite-reasoning.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · document

A claim at proved rank is universally quantified over an unbounded domain and its evidence describes a bounded range, with no proof or formal artifact cited.

**What the check does not establish.** Both halves are pattern matches over informal text, so findings are INFERRED. A claim whose universal quantification is implicit in prose and absent from the field is not caught, and a subtly incomplete reduction argument shows a proof evidence entry and stays quiet. What it reliably catches is the unguarded case: a big computation, a universal statement, and nothing in between.

### `computation.float-as-exact`

[Standard 10](../standards/10-computational-and-numerical-evidence.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · code-analysis

Evidence declaring exact arithmetic cites a program that uses floating-point arithmetic, or a claim of exact equality rests on a floating-point comparison.

**What the check does not establish.** A heuristic scan of the cited script for floating-point constructs, reported INFERRED. It cannot tell whether a float appears in the part of the program that matters, and it does not detect exactness claims resting on a computation that was never committed.

### `computation.reproducible-runs`

[Standard 10](../standards/10-computational-and-numerical-evidence.md) · recommended · warning · structural

A path-shaped artifact named by computational or numerical evidence resolves to a file in the repository.

**What the check does not establish.** Establishes that a file is present at the cited path. It does not run it, and does not check that the committed script is the one that produced the reported output.

### `computation.scope-declared`

[Standard 10](../standards/10-computational-and-numerical-evidence.md) · required · error · document

Evidence of type computational or numerical records the predicate checked, the range or sample, the arithmetic used, the program, the environment, any seed, and the outcome.

**What the check does not establish.** Looks for a bound and an arithmetic declaration in the evidence text. It cannot confirm that the program checked what the entry says it checked.

### `evidence.applicability-declared`

[Standard 1](../standards/01-applicability-and-scope.md) · required · warning · configuration

project-policy.yml declares which of the five regimes describe the project, and every not-applicable classification carries a reason and a revisitWhen condition.

**What the check does not establish.** Establishes that the declaration exists and is well-formed. It cannot tell whether the declaration is honest — a project that declares no formal regime while carrying Lean files is caught by formal.status-declared, but one that simply describes itself wrongly is not.

### `evidence.equivalence-direction-proved`

[Standard 15](../standards/15-equivalent-reformulations.md) · required · error · structural

An Equivalences entry claiming iff names a claim that proves the equivalence, and that claim resolves and is at proved rank.

**What the check does not establish.** Checks the declared direction and that the naming claim exists at proved rank. Whether the two statements really are equivalent is mathematics.

### `evidence.labels`

[Standard 19](../standards/19-evidence-requirements.md) · required · warning · document

Every finding carries one of OBSERVED, INFERRED, CONFIRMED_BY_OWNER, or UNKNOWN, and no heuristic detection is labelled OBSERVED.

**What the check does not establish.** Checks that every finding carries a label from the vocabulary. That each label is the right one for how the finding was produced is enforced by a test over the detectors, not by this rule at run time.

### `formal.axiom-disclosure`

[Standard 16](../standards/16-formal-theorem-proving.md) · required · error · code-analysis

An axiom declaration in a project proof-assistant source is listed in the axioms line of some claim's Formal block.

**What the check does not establish.** Scans comment- and string-stripped project sources for axiom declarations. It does not see axioms introduced by imported libraries, and it does not compute which declarations actually depend on a given axiom — only the assistant can do that.

### `formal.gap-inventory`

[Standard 16](../standards/16-formal-theorem-proving.md) · required · warning · document

Every claim carries a Formal field that is either a complete block or the token none, so the set of unformalised claims is explicit.

**What the check does not establish.** Establishes which claims declare formal status. The gap that matters most — whether the formal statement is the informal one, or an adjacent statement produced by modelling choices — is invisible here and is formal.statement-overclaim.

### `formal.placeholder-in-chain`

[Standard 16](../standards/16-formal-theorem-proving.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · code-analysis

A claim at FORMALIZED_THEOREM or MACHINE_CHECKED_PROOF cites a formal artifact that contains a placeholder token, cites no formal artifact, or cites a file that does not exist.

**What the check does not establish.** Establishes that a cited artifact contains a placeholder token, or that none is cited. It does NOT trace the dependency graph, so a clean pass is not certification — that requires running the assistant and committing the output of `#print axioms` or `Print Assumptions`. A .v file is treated as Coq only when it also contains Coq structure, because .v is equally a Verilog extension.

### `formal.placeholder-inventory`

[Standard 16](../standards/16-formal-theorem-proving.md) · recommended · warning · code-analysis

Placeholder tokens — sorry, admit, Admitted, oops — present in project proof-assistant sources are reported per file.

**What the check does not establish.** A token scan on comment- and string-stripped sources, so a comment reading 'remove the sorry' does not fire. It does not run the assistant and cannot see placeholders reached through dependencies the repository does not contain.

### `formal.status-declared`

[Standard 16](../standards/16-formal-theorem-proving.md) · required · warning · structural

Where .lean, .v, or .thy sources exist, at least one claim declares a Formal block referring to them, and the project declares the formal regime in its policy.

**What the check does not establish.** Observes that formal sources exist and that some claim mentions them. It does not check that every declaration in the development is accounted for.

### `formal.trusted-base-enlarged`

[Standard 16](../standards/16-formal-theorem-proving.md) · optional · info · code-analysis

Uses of native_decide, extern bindings, extraction, or code generation are reported so that the trusted base is visible.

**What the check does not establish.** Names known trusted-base-enlarging constructs found in project sources. It cannot enumerate the actual trusted base, which includes the kernel and every imported library.

### `formal.trusted-chain-tracked`

[Standard 16](../standards/16-formal-theorem-proving.md) · required · error · structural

A claim at FORMALIZED_THEOREM or MACHINE_CHECKED_PROOF carries a Formal block naming the assistant and version, the file, the declaration, the axioms, and the pinned external dependencies.

**What the check does not establish.** Checks that the fields are present and non-empty. It does not run the assistant, so it cannot verify that the recorded axiom list is the real one.

### `integrity.rule-lifecycle-honest`

[Standard 21](../standards/21-standards-integrity.md) · required · error · document

A rule is removed or weakened only via its deprecatedIn, supersededBy, and removedIn fields, together with a CHANGELOG entry and a MAJOR version bump.

**What the check does not establish.** Checks that lifecycle fields are present and internally consistent on the rules that exist. A rule deleted outright leaves nothing behind to check — the diff and the changelog are what make that visible, and judging whether the removal was justified is review.

### `lifecycle.failed-routes-preserved`

[Standard 18](../standards/18-research-lifecycle.md) · required · error · document

The project retains a location recording routes that were tried and abandoned, with what was tried and what happened.

**What the check does not establish.** Looks for a preserved-failure location. It cannot detect a deletion — nothing in a repository's current state reveals what was removed, and a check claiming otherwise would be inventing a capability.

### `lifecycle.reopening-evidence`

[Standard 18](../standards/18-research-lifecycle.md) · required · warning · document

Each terminated approach carries an 'Evidence required to reopen' line naming a specific, checkable condition.

**What the check does not establish.** Establishes that the line is present and non-empty. Whether the condition is specific enough to be checkable is review.

### `lifecycle.stopping-criteria`

[Standard 18](../standards/18-research-lifecycle.md) · required · warning · document

The research effort records what would make it stop: a barrier, a resource bound, a date, or a literature result that would settle the question.

**What the check does not establish.** Establishes that the section is non-empty. It cannot establish that the criteria were written in advance rather than reconstructed, which only the commit history shows.

### `lifecycle.terminated-approaches`

[Standard 18](../standards/18-research-lifecycle.md) · required · warning · document

Each terminated approach carries a Status line with its date and the reason it stopped.

**What the check does not establish.** Establishes that the line is present. The truthfulness of the reason is review.

### `literature.known-result-comparison`

[Standard 14](../standards/14-literature-and-novelty.md) · required · error · document

Before promotion to proved rank, a claim carries a record of what was searched and what was found — including a negative result and where it looked.

**What the check does not establish.** Establishes that a comparison was recorded. Whether the search was competent — whether it used the terms the field actually uses — is review.

### `literature.resolvable-identifiers`

[Standard 14](../standards/14-literature-and-novelty.md) · recommended · warning · structural

Every external: identifier used in a Depends or Assumptions field is defined in the ledger's References section, and any DOI or arXiv identifier there is well-formed.

**What the check does not establish.** Syntactic and offline. A well-formed identifier for a paper that does not exist passes. This repository makes no network calls during an audit and would not gain the right to merely because it would be convenient, so the rule catches malformed references and typos, and catches nothing of the failure Standard 14 is actually about.

### `literature.unchecked-novelty`

[Standard 14](../standards/14-literature-and-novelty.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · document

A claim asserts novelty and carries no citation-type evidence recording a prior-work search.

**What the check does not establish.** Matches novelty assertions in the claim's own text and checks for a recorded search. Novelty claimed in a paper draft rather than in the ledger is not seen, and the quality of the recorded search is not assessed.

### `problems.barriers-recorded`

[Standard 17](../standards/17-open-problems.md) · required · warning · document

The Known Barriers section records each barrier encountered, its citation, and which approaches it rules out.

**What the check does not establish.** Establishes that the section exists and says something. It cannot know which barriers apply to this problem.

### `problems.difficulty-location`

[Standard 17](../standards/17-open-problems.md) · required · error · document

The Where the Difficulty Lives section names, in plain language, what the hard part currently is, and what moved it when it has changed.

**What the check does not establish.** Establishes that the section is non-empty. Whether the answer is honest is proof.difficulty-displacement, which has no detector.

### `problems.equivalence-tracking`

[Standard 17](../standards/17-open-problems.md) · required · error · document

The Equivalences section records each relationship to the target with its direction — implies, implied-by, or iff — and the proof status of the relationship itself.

**What the check does not establish.** Establishes that the section is populated. Whether an asserted equivalence holds is mathematics.

### `problems.known-result-check`

[Standard 17](../standards/17-open-problems.md) · required · error · document

The Known Results section records the literature comparison, including prior attempts on this approach and why they stopped.

**What the check does not establish.** Establishes that the section is populated. The competence of the search is review.

### `problems.proved-vs-conjectural`

[Standard 17](../standards/17-open-problems.md) · required · error · structural

The What Is Proved and What Remains Conjectural sections are both present and non-empty.

**What the check does not establish.** Establishes that both sections say something. It does not cross-check them against the ledger's statuses, and it cannot tell an honest summary from an optimistic one.

### `proof.circular-dependency`

[Standard 8](../standards/08-dependency-traceability.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · structural

A claim appears in its own dependency closure, directly or through any chain of Depends and Assumptions edges.

**What the check does not establish.** Exact over the declared graph. A circular argument routed through an undeclared assumption produces no cycle here, and circularity inside a single proof text is invisible to a graph search.

### `proof.complete-with-open-obligations`

[Standard 7](../standards/07-proof-obligations.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · structural

A claim at LEMMA rank or above has at least one obligation whose state is open.

**What the check does not establish.** Exact over the obligations that were enumerated. An obligation nobody listed is not open, not discharged, and not visible.

### `proof.counterexample-search-recorded`

[Standard 9](../standards/09-edge-cases-and-counterexamples.md) · required · warning · document

A universally quantified claim above CONJECTURE rank carries evidence of type counterexample-search or proof.

**What the check does not establish.** Reads the declared evidence types. Warning-level because a claim with a complete proof does not need a search — the rule exists for the case where the proof is not there yet.

### `proof.dependency-traceability`

[Standard 8](../standards/08-dependency-traceability.md) · required · error · structural

Every identifier in a Depends or Assumptions field resolves to a ledger entry or to an external reference defined in the ledger's References section.

**What the check does not establish.** Exact over declared edges. A proof that uses a result it never cites has an undeclared edge, and no check sees it.

### `proof.obligations-enumerated`

[Standard 7](../standards/07-proof-obligations.md) · required · error · structural

Every claim at LEMMA rank or above carries an Obligations field, each obligation having an identifier, a statement, and a state of open or discharged.

**What the check does not establish.** Establishes that a list exists. It cannot establish that the list is complete: a proof with four obligations and three written down passes, and nothing in a text file knows about the fourth.

### `rigor.conjecture-registered`

[Standard 6](../standards/06-assumptions-and-hidden-conjectures.md) · required · error · document

Every identifier appearing in an Assumptions field resolves to a ledger entry or an external reference, rather than being named only in prose.

**What the check does not establish.** Checks that declared assumptions resolve. It cannot find an assumption that was never declared.

### `rigor.explicit-assumptions`

[Standard 6](../standards/06-assumptions-and-hidden-conjectures.md) · required · error · structural

Every claim at HYPOTHESIS rank or above carries an Assumptions field; `none` is an acceptable value and an omitted field is not.

**What the check does not establish.** Establishes that the field exists. Every downstream check that uses assumptions operates on what was declared; an assumption nobody wrote down is invisible to all of them.

### `rigor.explicit-domain`

[Standard 5](../standards/05-domains-and-quantifiers.md) · required · error · structural

Every claim at HYPOTHESIS rank or above carries a non-empty Domain field naming the set each free variable ranges over.

**What the check does not establish.** Establishes that a domain was stated. Whether the stated domain is the one the proof actually covers requires reading the proof, and is rigor.domain-restrictions-ignored.

### `rigor.explicit-quantifiers`

[Standard 5](../standards/05-domains-and-quantifiers.md) · required · error · document

Every claim at HYPOTHESIS rank or above carries a non-empty Quantifiers field, including the order of alternating quantifiers and any sufficiency qualifier.

**What the check does not establish.** Establishes that the field was filled in. It does not parse the quantifier structure or compare it against the proof.

## Requires expert judgement

Assurance `none`. Automation contributes vocabulary and an audit trail here, not verdicts. Each of these rules exists so that a reviewer has a named thing to check, a claimant has a named thing to attest to, and the coverage figure counts the gap instead of hiding it. They report `not-evaluated` in every automated run — never `passed`.

### `agent.refusal-on-invariant`

[Standard 22](../standards/22-ai-agent-operation.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

On a BLOCKED_BY_INVARIANT verdict, an agent edits the ledger, the policy, the catalog, or a detector to clear the block; reclassifies the rule as not applicable; writes an exception or attestation against it; or proceeds on the grounds that the blocked item is peripheral.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector. Nothing in a repository records whether an agent stopped when it should have: the evidence of compliance is an absence of work, and absences are not observable. What the framework supplies is an unambiguous signal to stop, an enumerated list of the available evasions so that taking one is a named violation rather than an improvisation, and a verdict none of them clears.

### `claims.reformulation-as-progress`

[Standard 15](../standards/15-equivalent-reformulations.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

A restatement of a claim is described as advancing it, on the strength of looking different rather than of changing what is proved or reducing to something strictly easier.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector. The structural consequence is caught by claims.status-exceeds-support — the target stays capped — but whether anyone is claiming otherwise in the prose, and whether the new form is genuinely more tractable, is a mathematician's judgement.

### `claims.silent-strengthening`

[Standard 5](../standards/05-domains-and-quantifiers.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

A claim's statement is broadened — a hypothesis dropped, a domain widened, a quantifier strengthened — without a history entry recording the change and without re-establishing the proof.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector. Deciding that one statement is strictly stronger than another is mathematics, not text comparison. Established by a reviewer comparing the statement against the proof, recorded as an attestation.

### `claims.silent-weakening`

[Standard 5](../standards/05-domains-and-quantifiers.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

A hypothesis is added or tightened so that a claim becomes provable, without the change being recorded and without dependent results being re-examined.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector, for the same reason as claims.silent-strengthening. A reviewer comparing statement revisions is what establishes it.

### `computation.cas-output-trust`

[Standard 13](../standards/13-symbolic-manipulation.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · warning · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

A CAS simplification, solution, or closed form is used without checking the validity conditions the system assumed and did not report.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector. Establishing which assumptions a simplification made requires re-deriving it.

### `computation.cherry-picking`

[Standard 10](../standards/10-computational-and-numerical-evidence.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

The reported computation describes the parameter ranges where the pattern held while omitting ranges that were tested and did not.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector and there cannot be one: selective reporting is a property of what was omitted, and omissions leave no artifact. Established by a reviewer comparing reported runs against the runs the repository still contains, which is why Standard 18 requires failures to be preserved.

### `evidence.discarded-failures`

[Standard 18](../standards/18-research-lifecycle.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

A run whose result tells against a hypothesis is deleted or omitted from the record.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector, for the same structural reason as evidence.hidden-counterexample. Established by review against the preserved-failures location Standard 18 requires.

### `evidence.hidden-counterexample`

[Standard 9](../standards/09-edge-cases-and-counterexamples.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

A discovered counterexample is not recorded, or the claim it refutes is not demoted.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector, and not for lack of effort: a suppressed counterexample leaves no trace in the repository, so there is nothing for a check to find. The defence is that Standard 18 requires failed routes to be preserved, making deletion a visible act rather than an absence.

### `formal.compile-as-proof`

[Standard 16](../standards/16-formal-theorem-proving.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

A development that builds is reported as proving the intended theorem, without establishing that the formal statement is the intended one.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector. Comparing a formal statement against an informal one is a question about the relationship between mathematics and its encoding, and nothing in the repository could answer it.

### `formal.helper-as-target`

[Standard 16](../standards/16-formal-theorem-proving.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

A checked auxiliary lemma is reported as establishing the target theorem, which remains unproved or placeholder-backed.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector for the reporting itself; formal.placeholder-in-chain catches the structural case where the target's cited artifact bears a placeholder.

### `formal.parse-as-proof`

[Standard 16](../standards/16-formal-theorem-proving.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

A syntactically valid proof-assistant file is reported as establishing a theorem.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector: this is a claim about what someone said, not about the repository's contents. Established by review of the project's own reporting.

### `formal.statement-overclaim`

[Standard 16](../standards/16-formal-theorem-proving.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

A machine-checked declaration is described as establishing a stronger, more general, or differently quantified statement than the one it formalises.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector, and no prospect of one. Established by a reviewer who reads both the formal statement and the claim.

### `integrity.no-self-serving-modification`

[Standard 21](../standards/21-standards-integrity.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

A human or AI bypasses, weakens, removes, reclassifies, reinterprets, falsifies evidence for, or manipulates a standard, test, applicability determination, evidence requirement, or verification mechanism solely because it prevents the desired implementation or conclusion.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector, and this is the most important assurance note in the catalog. The mechanisms of Standard 21 R4 — provenance digests, the committed inventory, fidelity checking, non-exemptible rejection, the attestation contradiction check, the lifecycle and changelog trail, and the mutation checks — each make a specific manipulation fail. None of them observes motive, and motive is what this rule is about. Every one of them is also defeated by a single commit that changes the guard and the guarded thing together; what they buy is that such a commit is loud. The residual protection is review, and the residual risk is a determined author with no reviewer.

### `literature.citation-statement-drift`

[Standard 14](../standards/14-literature-and-novelty.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

A real, resolvable reference is cited for a statement stronger than the one it establishes — an extra hypothesis dropped, a domain widened, a conclusion strengthened.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector, and literature.resolvable-identifiers passing is not evidence against it. Established only by a person comparing the cited theorem against the use made of it.

### `literature.fabricated-citation`

[Standard 14](../standards/14-literature-and-novelty.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

A cited work does not exist, or an asserted known result is not in the literature.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector. Establishing existence requires resolving the reference against the world, which an offline checker cannot do. Established by a person opening the paper, recorded as an attestation.

### `problems.restatement-as-solution`

[Standard 17](../standards/17-open-problems.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

A restatement of the central conjecture is described as solving it.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector. The structural signal — the target's status stays capped by its dependency closure — is caught by claims.status-exceeds-support, but the claim of having solved the problem lives in prose and its assessment is mathematical.

### `proof.difficulty-displacement`

[Standard 7](../standards/07-proof-obligations.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

The unresolved difficulty is relocated into a newly defined lemma, and progress is claimed on the grounds that the main theorem follows from that lemma.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector. The structural half is caught by claims.status-exceeds-support — the target stays capped by its conjectural lemma. Whether the new lemma is the original difficulty wearing a hat, or a genuine decomposition, needs a mathematician.

### `proof.edge-cases-addressed`

[Standard 9](../standards/09-edge-cases-and-counterexamples.md) · required · warning · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

The empty case, the smallest cases, the trivial object, the boundary of the domain, and equality in strict inequalities are addressed rather than left implicit.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector. Knowing which cases are degenerate for a given claim is knowing the mathematics.

### `proof.existence-as-construction`

[Standard 20](../standards/20-must-never-rules.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

A nonconstructive existence result is stated or used as though an explicit object, algorithm, or bound had been exhibited.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector. Whether a proof is constructive is a property of the argument.

### `proof.induction-gaps`

[Standard 20](../standards/20-must-never-rules.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

An induction omits its base case, uses a base case that does not establish the claimed starting point, or uses a step that fails for small values of the index.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector. Established by a reviewer, or by formalising the induction, which cannot be completed with a missing base case.

### `proof.unjustified-triviality`

[Standard 6](../standards/06-assumptions-and-hidden-conjectures.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · warning · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

A triviality marker — clearly, obviously, trivially, it is well known that, one easily sees — stands in for a nontrivial proof obligation that is never enumerated.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector. Finding the words is trivial and useless; deciding whether what they cover is genuinely routine is the mathematics.

### `rigor.almost-all-as-all`

[Standard 11](../standards/11-finite-and-infinite-reasoning.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

A density-one, almost-everywhere, generic, or probability-one result is used or restated as holding for all cases, or at a particular case of interest.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector. rigor.explicit-quantifiers requires the qualifier to be recorded; noticing that a later passage dropped it is review.

### `rigor.domain-restrictions-ignored`

[Standard 5](../standards/05-domains-and-quantifiers.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

A claim is stated or used on a domain larger than the one its proof covers.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector. rigor.explicit-domain establishes that a domain was stated; comparing it against the proof's actual coverage is mathematics.

### `rigor.hidden-assumption`

[Standard 6](../standards/06-assumptions-and-hidden-conjectures.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

A result relies on a statement that is neither proved nor declared in its Assumptions field.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector and there cannot be one: the whole content of the rule is about something absent from the record. Established by a mathematician reading the proof and asking what it uses.

### `rigor.notation-equivocation`

[Standard 13](../standards/13-symbolic-manipulation.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · warning · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

The same symbol or term is used with two meanings within one argument, so that each step is valid under some reading and no single consistent reading validates all of them.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector. Establishing it requires tracking what each symbol denotes at each step, which is reading the mathematics.

### `rigor.symbolic-validity-conditions`

[Standard 13](../standards/13-symbolic-manipulation.md) · required · warning · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

Each nontrivial manipulation — cancellation, root extraction, rearrangement, matrix inversion — states the condition under which it is valid, and that condition is a discharged obligation or a declared assumption.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector, deliberately. A rule flagging every division would produce noise a project would suppress, and a suppressed rule still counts in coverage. Established by a mathematician or by a proof assistant that refuses the step.

### `rigor.unjustified-division`

[Standard 13](../standards/13-symbolic-manipulation.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

A proof divides by, or cancels, an expression without establishing that the expression is non-zero throughout the domain.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector. Whether a denominator can vanish on the domain is the mathematics, not a property of the text.

### `rigor.unjustified-interchange`

[Standard 13](../standards/13-symbolic-manipulation.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · error · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

A proof exchanges the order of limits, sums, derivatives, or integrals without the uniformity, convergence, or domination hypothesis that makes the exchange valid.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector. Established by a mathematician, or by formalising the step in a proof assistant, which cannot proceed without the hypothesis.

### `rigor.wlog-abuse`

[Standard 20](../standards/20-must-never-rules.md) · forbidden (invariant — no exception reaches it) · warning · manual-review · **not evaluated by any detector**

A WLOG reduction discards a case that is not in fact equivalent to the case kept, by a symmetry that is assumed rather than established.

**What the check does not establish.** No detector. Established by a reviewer checking that the claimed symmetry holds.

## The short version

**What this system reliably prevents.** A claim status outside the fifteen-token vocabulary. A
status that disagrees with its own recorded history. A claim at proved rank whose declared
dependencies include a conjecture. A dependency cycle — the target theorem assumed in its own
proof, however many lemmas the route passes through. A claim at proved rank with an open
obligation. A claim whose only declared evidence is computational. A universal statement supported
by a bounded check. A `MACHINE_CHECKED_PROOF` citing a file that contains `sorry`, or citing
nothing, or citing a file that does not exist. An undisclosed axiom. An open-problem record with
an unanswered section. Evidence pointing at a file that is not there. A source prompt edited after
the fact. And — the rule the rest protect — a rule nothing evaluated being reported as passing.

**What still requires a mathematician.** Whether a proof is correct. Whether an assumption was
used and never declared, which is what makes it hidden. Whether a symbolic step's validity
condition holds. Whether a stated domain is the domain the proof covers. Whether a citation says
what it is cited for. Whether a counterexample was found and suppressed, or a failed run deleted —
both leave no artifact, by construction. Whether a reformulation is progress or the same
difficulty renamed. Whether a formal statement is the theorem the paper claims. And whether any
particular change to a standard was made because the standard was wrong or because it was in the
way.

The second list is not a backlog. Several of its entries are unmechanisable in principle, and
saying so is a requirement of the standards themselves: a tool that overstated its own coverage
would be committing the error it exists to prevent.
